subject: common-workplace-fundamentals
summary: Explains the key perspectives for conducting code reviews, how to write constructive comments, and how to respond to review feedback professionally.
key_points: Review for correctness, readability, maintainability, security, and performance.
Constructive comments include what is wrong, why it matters, and how to fix it.
Treat feedback as directed at the code, not at you personally.
misconceptions: Code review is only about formatting and naming conventions.
All review comments carry the same level of importance.
Disagreeing with a review comment is unprofessional.
check_questions: What are the five main perspectives to check during code review?
What three elements should a constructive review comment contain?
How should you respond when you disagree with a review comment?

fact_candidates: Five categories of code review focus (correctness, readability, maintainability, security, performance)
practical_judgment_candidates: Distinguishing a constructive comment from a vague or unhelpful one
Deciding whether a review comment warrants a code change or a discussion
error_interpretation_candidates: Identifying what makes a review comment vague and how to improve it
scenario_candidates: Vague performance complaint with no specific cause or suggestion
Security-critical SQL injection finding marked as [must]
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Believing that only formatting issues matter in code review
Treating review feedback as a personal attack rather than code feedback
